rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes laser-based cold spraying, whereas the study used SPS-consolidated high-entropy-alloy electrodes followed by electrospark deposition, so it captures a nontraditional coating repair concept but uses a different deposition route and omits the consolidation lever.
rationale.condition_agreement: The proposed aggressive service conditions of up to 500 °C and 500 MPa were not tested; the study instead specified SPS and argon-shielded ESD processing conditions and performed no aggressive-environment service testing.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis relies on avoiding high-temperature metallurgical reactions, while the study relied on SPS diffusion and densification followed by pulsed-spark melting, substrate mixing, rapid solidification, and layer-dependent residual-stress defects.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The predicted reduction in hot cracking and increase in service life versus fusion welding were not measured; the actual outcomes concerned electrode densification, hardness, coating continuity, oxidation, porosity, roughness, microfissuring, and a six-layer deposition limit.
